writerNotes: lesson: the hero writes out one lesson in an exercise book. Pick a topic the tutor teaches, a real question a student might be stuck on, the big idea in one short sentence, a sketch that fits (fractions, triangle, wave, or none), one to three lines of a worked example, then a similar question they try, a line with a believable slip, the fix and the right line. Keep every line short (it is handwritten on a page). Minutes, tries and the score are for one lesson.
report: the four labels; the confidence word at the start and at the end of the lesson. stages: six steps in the tutor's voice.
subjects.list: the brief's subjects with the levels it gives, each with a colour and a short sign (a letter, number or symbol that works in handwriting).
price: the brief's rates by level exactly, its lesson lengths and how often (lessons per week), and the weeks in a term (12 if not given).

trial: the times a first lesson can start, the brief's tutors (or one entry for the tutor), and only qualifications the brief gives. The booking form really sends: the request goes to the tutors, who confirm it. Never say it is booked, paid or confirmed.

hero.title and hero.titleEm: a short two-part headline (four lines at most on a desktop); section titles have a second half. theme.accent is the tutor's colour (also the red pen), deep enough for white button text; theme.wordmarkFit is always "fit".
business.name is set to exactly the name in the brief and cannot be changed; brand.name is how it appears in the nav and the footer (short).
